claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting microstructure consists of FCC and B2 phases.
The as-cast alloy has strength and ductility below fastener-application requirements.
The proposed intervention is post-casting annealing at approximately 700°C for 2–4 hours in inert gas or vacuum.
The proposed annealing treatment will form L12 precipitates within the FCC lamellae.
The induced L12 precipitates will be nanoscale, coherent, uniformly distributed, and resistant to coarsening under the specified treatment.
The precipitated microstructure will maintain strong interfacial bonding with adjacent phases.
The coherent L12 precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion through the Orowan mechanism.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the precipitates will increase yield strength.
The precipitates will improve resistance to room-temperature creep and prolonged mechanical loading.
A fine, uniform precipitate dispersion will minimize stress concentrations and preserve ductility.
The treated alloy will remain mechanically stable during cyclic loading and extreme temperature fluctuations.
The treatment will maintain the alloy's inherent corrosion resistance.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, annealing is expected to produce a significant increase in yield strength.
Relative to the as-cast alloy, annealing is expected to reduce creep rate while retaining at least 90% of baseline ductility.
Deviation from the optimized annealing schedule may cause over-aging and precipitate coarsening.
Precipitate coarsening caused by over-aging will compromise mechanical performance.
